133/*
134 * cgroup_event represents events which userspace want to receive.
135 */
136struct mem_cgroup_event {
137 /*
138 * memcg which the event belongs to.
139 */
140 struct mem_cgroup *memcg;
141 /*
142 * eventfd to signal userspace about the event.
143 */
144 struct eventfd_ctx *eventfd;
145 /*
146 * Each of these stored in a list by the cgroup.
147 */
148 struct list_head list;
149 /*
150 * register_event() callback will be used to add new userspace
151 * waiter for changes related to this event. Use eventfd_signal()
152 * on eventfd to send notification to userspace.
153 */
154 int (*register_event)(struct mem_cgroup *memcg,
155 struct eventfd_ctx *eventfd, const char *args);
156 /*
157 * unregister_event() callback will be called when userspace closes
158 * the eventfd or on cgroup removing. This callback must be set,
159 * if you want provide notification functionality.
160 */
161 void (*unregister_event)(struct mem_cgroup *memcg,
162 struct eventfd_ctx *eventfd);
163 /*
164 * All fields below needed to unregister event when
165 * userspace closes eventfd.
166 */
167 poll_table pt;
168 wait_queue_head_t *wqh;
169 wait_queue_entry_t wait;
170 struct work_struct remove;
171};

275 /*
276 * At this point all allocated objects are freed, and
277 * objcg->nr_charged_bytes can't have an arbitrary byte value.
278 * However, it can be PAGE_SIZE or (x * PAGE_SIZE).
279 *
280 * The following sequence can lead to it:
281 * 1) CPU0: objcg == stock->cached_objcg
282 * 2) CPU1: we do a small allocation (e.g. 92 bytes),
283 * PAGE_SIZE bytes are charged
284 * 3) CPU1: a process from another memcg is allocating something,
285 * the stock if flushed,
286 * objcg->nr_charged_bytes = PAGE_SIZE - 92
287 * 5) CPU0: we do release this object,
288 * 92 bytes are added to stock->nr_bytes
289 * 6) CPU0: stock is flushed,
290 * 92 bytes are added to objcg->nr_charged_bytes
291 *
292 * In the result, nr_charged_bytes == PAGE_SIZE.
293 * This page will be uncharged in obj_cgroup_release().
294 */

385/**
386 * page_cgroup_ino - return inode number of the memcg a page is charged to
387 * @page: the page
388 *
389 * Look up the closest online ancestor of the memory cgroup @page is charged to
390 * and return its inode number or 0 if @page is not charged to any cgroup. It
391 * is safe to call this function without holding a reference to @page.
392 *
393 * Note, this function is inherently racy, because there is nothing to prevent
394 * the cgroup inode from getting torn down and potentially reallocated a moment
395 * after page_cgroup_ino() returns, so it only should be used by callers that
396 * do not care (such as procfs interfaces).
397 */

399{
400 struct mem_cgroup *memcg;
401 unsigned long ino = 0;
402
403 rcu_read_lock();
404 /* page_folio() is racy here, but the entire function is racy anyway */
405 memcg = folio_memcg_check(page_folio(page)(_Generic((page), const struct page *: (const struct folio *)
_compound_head(page), struct page *: (struct folio *)_compound_head
(page))));
406
407 while (memcg && !(memcg->css.flags & CSS_ONLINE))
408 memcg = parent_mem_cgroup(memcg);
409 if (memcg)
410 ino = cgroup_ino(memcg->css.cgroup);
411 rcu_read_unlock();
412 return ino;
413}

485static void mem_cgroup_update_tree(struct mem_cgroup *memcg, int nid)
486{
487 unsigned long excess;
488 struct mem_cgroup_per_node *mz;
489 struct mem_cgroup_tree_per_node *mctz;
490
491 if (lru_gen_enabled()) {
492 if (soft_limit_excess(memcg))
493 lru_gen_soft_reclaim(memcg, nid);
494 return;
495 }
496
497 mctz = soft_limit_tree.rb_tree_per_node[nid];
498 if (!mctz)
499 return;
500 /*
501 * Necessary to update all ancestors when hierarchy is used.
502 * because their event counter is not touched.
503 */
504 for (; memcg; memcg = parent_mem_cgroup(memcg)) {
505 mz = memcg->nodeinfo[nid];
506 excess = soft_limit_excess(memcg);
507 /*
508 * We have to update the tree if mz is on RB-tree or
509 * mem is over its softlimit.
510 */
511 if (excess || mz->on_tree) {
512 unsigned long flags;
513
514 spin_lock_irqsave(&mctz->lock, flags)do { do { ({ unsigned long __dummy; typeof(flags) __dummy2; (
void)(&__dummy == &__dummy2); 1; }); flags = _raw_spin_lock_irqsave
(spinlock_check(&mctz->lock)); } while (0); } while (0
);
515 /* if on-tree, remove it */
516 if (mz->on_tree)
517 __mem_cgroup_remove_exceeded(mz, mctz);
518 /*
519 * Insert again. mz->usage_in_excess will be updated.
520 * If excess is 0, no tree ops.
521 */
522 __mem_cgroup_insert_exceeded(mz, mctz, excess);
523 spin_unlock_irqrestore(&mctz->lock, flags);
524 }
525 }
526}

664/*
665 * memcg and lruvec stats flushing
666 *
667 * Many codepaths leading to stats update or read are performance sensitive and
668 * adding stats flushing in such codepaths is not desirable. So, to optimize the
669 * flushing the kernel does:
670 *
671 * 1) Periodically and asynchronously flush the stats every 2 seconds to not let
672 * rstat update tree grow unbounded.
673 *
674 * 2) Flush the stats synchronously on reader side only when there are more than
675 * (MEMCG_CHARGE_BATCH * nr_cpus) update events. Though this optimization
676 * will let stats be out of sync by atmost (MEMCG_CHARGE_BATCH * nr_cpus) but
677 * only for 2 seconds due to (1).
678 */

748/*
749 * mem_cgroup_flush_stats - flush the stats of a memory cgroup subtree
750 * @memcg: root of the subtree to flush
751 *
752 * Flushing is serialized by the underlying global rstat lock. There is also a
753 * minimum amount of work to be done even if there are no stat updates to flush.
754 * Hence, we only flush the stats if the updates delta exceeds a threshold. This
755 * avoids unnecessary work and contention on the underlying lock.
756 */
757void mem_cgroup_flush_stats(struct mem_cgroup *memcg)
758{
759 if (mem_cgroup_disabled())
760 return;
761
762 if (!memcg)
763 memcg = root_mem_cgroup;
764
765 if (memcg_vmstats_needs_flush(memcg->vmstats))
766 do_flush_stats(memcg);
767}

780 * in latency-sensitive paths is as cheap as possible.

880/**
881 * __mod_lruvec_state - update lruvec memory statistics
882 * @lruvec: the lruvec
883 * @idx: the stat item
884 * @val: delta to add to the counter, can be negative
885 *
886 * The lruvec is the intersection of the NUMA node and a cgroup. This
887 * function updates the all three counters that are affected by a
888 * change of state at this level: per-node, per-cgroup, per-lruvec.
889 */
890void __mod_lruvec_state(struct lruvec *lruvec, enum node_stat_item idx,
891 int val)
892{
893 /* Update node */
894 __mod_node_page_state(lruvec_pgdat(lruvec), idx, val);
895
896 /* Update memcg and lruvec */
897 if (!mem_cgroup_disabled())
898 __mod_memcg_lruvec_state(lruvec, idx, val);
899}
900
901void __lruvec_stat_mod_folio(struct folio *folio, enum node_stat_item idx,
902 int val)
903{
904 struct mem_cgroup *memcg;
905 pg_data_t *pgdat = folio_pgdat(folio);
906 struct lruvec *lruvec;
907
908 rcu_read_lock();
909 memcg = folio_memcg(folio);
910 /* Untracked pages have no memcg, no lruvec. Update only the node */
911 if (!memcg) {
912 rcu_read_unlock();
913 __mod_node_page_state(pgdat, idx, val);
914 return;
915 }
916
917 lruvec = mem_cgroup_lruvec(memcg, pgdat);
918 __mod_lruvec_state(lruvec, idx, val);
919 rcu_read_unlock();
920}

1286static void invalidate_reclaim_iterators(struct mem_cgroup *dead_memcg)
1287{
1288 struct mem_cgroup *memcg = dead_memcg;
1289 struct mem_cgroup *last;
1290
1291 do {
1292 __invalidate_reclaim_iterators(memcg, dead_memcg);
1293 last = memcg;
1294 } while ((memcg = parent_mem_cgroup(memcg)));
1295
1296 /*
1297 * When cgroup1 non-hierarchy mode is used,
1298 * parent_mem_cgroup() does not walk all the way up to the
1299 * cgroup root (root_mem_cgroup). So we have to handle
1300 * dead_memcg from cgroup root separately.
1301 */
1302 if (!mem_cgroup_is_root(last))
1303 __invalidate_reclaim_iterators(root_mem_cgroup,
1304 dead_memcg);
1305}

1362 * @folio: Pointer to the folio.
1363 *
1364 * These functions are safe to use under any of the following conditions:
1365 * - folio locked
1366 * - folio_test_lru false
1367 * - folio_memcg_lock()
1368 * - folio frozen (refcount of 0)
1369 *
1370 * Return: The lruvec this folio is on with its lock held.
1371 */

1373{
1374 struct lruvec *lruvec = folio_lruvec(folio);

1376 spin_lock(&lruvec->lru_lock);
1377 lruvec_memcg_debug(lruvec, folio);

1379 return lruvec;

1498/*
1499 * A routine for checking "mem" is under move_account() or not.
1500 *
1501 * Checking a cgroup is mc.from or mc.to or under hierarchy of
1502 * moving cgroups. This is for waiting at high-memory pressure
1503 * caused by "move".
1504 */
1505static bool mem_cgroup_under_move(struct mem_cgroup *memcg)
1506{
1507 struct mem_cgroup *from;
1508 struct mem_cgroup *to;
1509 bool ret = false;
1510 /*
1511 * Unlike task_move routines, we access mc.to, mc.from not under
1512 * mutual exclusion by cgroup_mutex. Here, we take spinlock instead.
1513 */
1514 spin_lock(&mc.lock);
1515 from = mc.from;
1516 to = mc.to;
1517 if (!from)
1518 goto unlock;
1519
1520 ret = mem_cgroup_is_descendant(from, memcg) ||
1521 mem_cgroup_is_descendant(to, memcg);
1522unlock:
1523 spin_unlock(&mc.lock);
1524 return ret;
1525}
1526
1527static bool mem_cgroup_wait_acct_move(struct mem_cgroup *memcg)
1528{
1529 if (mc.moving_task && currentget_current() != mc.moving_task) {
1530 if (mem_cgroup_under_move(memcg)) {
1531 DEFINE_WAIT(wait)struct wait_queue_entry wait = { .private = get_current(), .func
= autoremove_wake_function, .entry = { &((wait).entry), &
((wait).entry) }, };
1532 prepare_to_wait(&mc.waitq, &wait, TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE0x00000001);
1533 /* moving charge context might have finished. */
1534 if (mc.moving_task)
1535 schedule();
1536 finish_wait(&mc.waitq, &wait);
1537 return true;
1538 }
1539 }
1540 return false;
1541}

1592/* The actual unit of the state item, not the same as the output unit */
1593static int memcg_page_state_unit(int item)
1594{
1595 switch (item) {
1596 case MEMCG_PERCPU_B:
1597 case MEMCG_ZSWAP_B:
1598 case NR_SLAB_RECLAIMABLE_B:
1599 case NR_SLAB_UNRECLAIMABLE_B:
1600 return 1;
1601 case NR_KERNEL_STACK_KB:
1602 return SZ_1K0x00000400;
1603 default:
1604 return PAGE_SIZE((1UL) << 12);
1605 }
1606}
1607
1608/* Translate stat items to the correct unit for memory.stat output */
1609static int memcg_page_state_output_unit(int item)
1610{
1611 /*
1612 * Workingset state is actually in pages, but we export it to userspace
1613 * as a scalar count of events, so special case it here.
1614 */
1615 switch (item) {
1616 case WORKINGSET_REFAULT_ANON:
1617 case WORKINGSET_REFAULT_FILE:
1618 case WORKINGSET_ACTIVATE_ANON:
1619 case WORKINGSET_ACTIVATE_FILE:
1620 case WORKINGSET_RESTORE_ANON:
1621 case WORKINGSET_RESTORE_FILE:
1622 case WORKINGSET_NODERECLAIM:
1623 return 1;
1624 default:
1625 return memcg_page_state_unit(item);
1626 }
1627}
1628
1629static inlineinline __attribute__((__gnu_inline__)) __attribute__((__unused__
)) __attribute__((no_instrument_function)) unsigned long memcg_page_state_output(struct mem_cgroup *memcg,
1630 int item)
1631{
1632 return memcg_page_state(memcg, item) *
1633 memcg_page_state_output_unit(item);
1634}

1636static inlineinline __attribute__((__gnu_inline__)) __attribute__((__unused__
)) __attribute__((no_instrument_function)) unsigned long memcg_page_state_local_output(
1637 struct mem_cgroup *memcg, int item)
1638{
1639 return memcg_page_state_local(memcg, item) *
1640 memcg_page_state_output_unit(item);
1641}

1643static void memcg_stat_format(struct mem_cgroup *memcg, struct seq_buf *s)
1644{
1645 int i;
1646
1647 /*
1648 * Provide statistics on the state of the memory subsystem as
1649 * well as cumulative event counters that show past behavior.
1650 *
1651 * This list is ordered following a combination of these gradients:
1652 * 1) generic big picture -> specifics and details
1653 * 2) reflecting userspace activity -> reflecting kernel heuristics
1654 *
1655 * Current memory state:
1656 */
1657 mem_cgroup_flush_stats(memcg);

1659 for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(memory_stats)(sizeof(memory_stats) / sizeof((memory_stats)[0]) + ((int)(sizeof
(struct { int:(-!!(__builtin_types_compatible_p(typeof((memory_stats
)), typeof(&(memory_stats)[0])))); })))); i++) {
1660 u64 size;
1661
1662 size = memcg_page_state_output(memcg, memory_stats[i].idx);
1663 seq_buf_printf(s, "%s %llu\n", memory_stats[i].name, size);
1664
1665 if (unlikely(memory_stats[i].idx == NR_SLAB_UNRECLAIMABLE_B)__builtin_expect(!!(memory_stats[i].idx == NR_SLAB_UNRECLAIMABLE_B
), 0)) {

1674 memcg_events(memcg, PGSCAN_KSWAPD) +
1675 memcg_events(memcg, PGSCAN_DIRECT) +

1681
1682 for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(memcg_vm_event_stat)(sizeof(memcg_vm_event_stat) / sizeof((memcg_vm_event_stat)[0
]) + ((int)(sizeof(struct { int:(-!!(__builtin_types_compatible_p
(typeof((memcg_vm_event_stat)), typeof(&(memcg_vm_event_stat
)[0])))); })))); i++) {
1683 if (memcg_vm_event_stat[i] == PGPGIN ||
1684 memcg_vm_event_stat[i] == PGPGOUT)
1685 continue;
1686
1687 seq_buf_printf(s, "%s %lu\n",
1688 vm_event_name(memcg_vm_event_stat[i]),
1689 memcg_events(memcg, memcg_vm_event_stat[i]));
1690 }

1796static bool mem_cgroup_out_of_memory(struct mem_cgroup *memcg, gfp_t gfp_mask,
1797 int order)
1798{
1799 struct oom_control oc = {
1800 .zonelist = NULL((void *)0),
1801 .nodemask = NULL((void *)0),
1802 .memcg = memcg,
1803 .gfp_mask = gfp_mask,
1804 .order = order,
1805 };
1806 bool ret = true;
1807
1808 if (mutex_lock_killable(&oom_lock)mutex_lock_killable_nested(&oom_lock, 0))
1809 return true;
1810
1811 if (mem_cgroup_margin(memcg) >= (1 << order))
1812 goto unlock;
1813
1814 /*
1815 * A few threads which were not waiting at mutex_lock_killable() can
1816 * fail to bail out. Therefore, check again after holding oom_lock.
1817 */
1818 ret = task_is_dying() || out_of_memory(&oc);
1819
1820unlock:
1821 mutex_unlock(&oom_lock);
1822 return ret;
1823}

1825static int mem_cgroup_soft_reclaim(struct mem_cgroup *root_memcg,
1826 pg_data_t *pgdat,
1827 gfp_t gfp_mask,
1828 unsigned long *total_scanned)
1829{
1830 struct mem_cgroup *victim = NULL((void *)0);
1831 int total = 0;
1832 int loop = 0;
1833 unsigned long excess;
1834 unsigned long nr_scanned;
1835 struct mem_cgroup_reclaim_cookie reclaim = {
1836 .pgdat = pgdat,
1837 };
1838
1839 excess = soft_limit_excess(root_memcg);
1840
1841 while (1) {
1842 victim = mem_cgroup_iter(root_memcg, victim, &reclaim);
1843 if (!victim) {
1844 loop++;
1845 if (loop >= 2) {
1846 /*
1847 * If we have not been able to reclaim
1848 * anything, it might because there are
1849 * no reclaimable pages under this hierarchy
1850 */
1851 if (!total)
1852 break;
1853 /*
1854 * We want to do more targeted reclaim.
1855 * excess >> 2 is not to excessive so as to
1856 * reclaim too much, nor too less that we keep
1857 * coming back to reclaim from this cgroup
1858 */
1859 if (total >= (excess >> 2) ||
1860 (loop > MEM_CGROUP_MAX_RECLAIM_LOOPS100))
1861 break;
1862 }
1863 continue;
1864 }
1865 total += mem_cgroup_shrink_node(victim, gfp_mask, false,
1866 pgdat, &nr_scanned);
1867 *total_scanned += nr_scanned;
1868 if (!soft_limit_excess(root_memcg))
1869 break;
1870 }
1871 mem_cgroup_iter_break(root_memcg, victim);
1872 return total;
1873}

1884 * Check OOM-Killer is already running under our hierarchy.
1885 * If someone is running, return false.

1896 * this subtree of our hierarchy is already locked

1911 for_each_mem_cgroup_tree(iter, memcg)for (iter = mem_cgroup_iter(memcg, ((void *)0), ((void *)0));
iter != ((void *)0); iter = mem_cgroup_iter(memcg, iter, ((void
*)0))) {
1912 if (iter == failed) {
1913 mem_cgroup_iter_break(memcg, iter);
1914 break;

1918 } else
1919 mutex_acquire(&memcg_oom_lock_dep_map, 0, 1, _RET_IP_)lock_acquire(&memcg_oom_lock_dep_map, 0, 1, 0, 1, ((void *
)0), (unsigned long)__builtin_return_address(0));
1920
1921 spin_unlock(&memcg_oom_lock);
1922
1923 return !failed;

1937static void mem_cgroup_mark_under_oom(struct mem_cgroup *memcg)
1938{
1939 struct mem_cgroup *iter;

1941 spin_lock(&memcg_oom_lock);
1942 for_each_mem_cgroup_tree(iter, memcg)for (iter = mem_cgroup_iter(memcg, ((void *)0), ((void *)0));

1947static void mem_cgroup_unmark_under_oom(struct mem_cgroup *memcg)
1948{
1949 struct mem_cgroup *iter;

1951 /*
1952 * Be careful about under_oom underflows because a child memcg
1953 * could have been added after mem_cgroup_mark_under_oom.

iter != ((void *)0); iter = mem_cgroup_iter(memcg, iter, ((void
*)0)))
1957 if (iter->under_oom > 0)
1958 iter->under_oom--;
1959 spin_unlock(&memcg_oom_lock);
1960}

1985static void memcg_oom_recover(struct mem_cgroup *memcg)
1986{
1987 /*
1988 * For the following lockless ->under_oom test, the only required
1989 * guarantee is that it must see the state asserted by an OOM when
1990 * this function is called as a result of userland actions
1991 * triggered by the notification of the OOM. This is trivially
1992 * achieved by invoking mem_cgroup_mark_under_oom() before
1993 * triggering notification.
1994 */
1995 if (memcg && memcg->under_oom)
1996 __wake_up(&memcg_oom_waitq, TASK_NORMAL(0x00000001 | 0x00000002), 0, memcg);
1997}
1998
1999/*
2000 * Returns true if successfully killed one or more processes. Though in some
2001 * corner cases it can return true even without killing any process.
2002 */
2003static bool mem_cgroup_oom(struct mem_cgroup *memcg, gfp_t mask, int order)
2004{
2005 bool locked, ret;
2006
2007 if (order > PAGE_ALLOC_COSTLY_ORDER3)
2008 return false;
2009
2010 memcg_memory_event(memcg, MEMCG_OOM);
2011
2012 /*
2013 * We are in the middle of the charge context here, so we
2014 * don't want to block when potentially sitting on a callstack

2494/*
2495 * Clamp the maximum sleep time per allocation batch to 2 seconds. This is
2496 * enough to still cause a significant slowdown in most cases, while still
2497 * allowing diagnostics and tracing to proceed without becoming stuck.

2503 * maintain precision and scale to a reasonable number of jiffies (see the table
2504 * below.
2505 *

2507 * overage ratio to a delay.
2508 * - MEMCG_DELAY_SCALING_SHIFT: The number of bits to scale down the
2509 * proposed penalty in order to reduce to a reasonable number of jiffies, and
2510 * to produce a reasonable delay curve.

2513 * reasonable delay curve compared to precision-adjusted overage, not

2515 * limit penalises misbehaviour cgroups by slowing them down exponentially. For
2516 * example, with a high of 100 megabytes:

2595/*
2596 * Get the number of jiffies that we should penalise a mischievous cgroup which
2597 * is exceeding its memory.high by checking both it and its ancestors.
2598 */
2599static unsigned long calculate_high_delay(struct mem_cgroup *memcg,
2600 unsigned int nr_pages,
2601 u64 max_overage)
2602{
2603 unsigned long penalty_jiffies;

2606 return 0;
2607
2608 /*
2609 * We use overage compared to memory.high to calculate the number of
2610 * jiffies to sleep (penalty_jiffies). Ideally this value should be
2611 * fairly lenient on small overages, and increasingly harsh when the
2612 * memcg in question makes it clear that it has no intention of stopping
2613 * its crazy behaviour, so we exponentially increase the delay based on
2614 * overage amount.

2616 penalty_jiffies = max_overage * max_overage * HZ250;
2617 penalty_jiffies >>= MEMCG_DELAY_PRECISION_SHIFT20;
2618 penalty_jiffies >>= MEMCG_DELAY_SCALING_SHIFT14;
2619
2620 /*
2621 * Factor in the task's own contribution to the overage, such that four
2622 * N-sized allocations are throttled approximately the same as one
2623 * 4N-sized allocation.
2624 *
2625 * MEMCG_CHARGE_BATCH pages is nominal, so work out how much smaller or
2626 * larger the current charge patch is than that.
2627 */
2628 return penalty_jiffies * nr_pages / MEMCG_CHARGE_BATCH64U;

3020 return NULL((void *)0);

3030 return folio_memcg_check(folio);

3033/*

3037 * kernel page, so different mechanisms for getting the memory cgroup pointer

folio *)_compound_head(vmalloc_to_page(p)), struct page *: (
struct folio *)_compound_head(vmalloc_to_page(p))));

3509int obj_cgroup_charge(struct obj_cgroup *objcg, gfp_t gfp, size_t size)
3510{
3511 unsigned int nr_pages, nr_bytes;
3512 int ret;
3513
3514 if (consume_obj_stock(objcg, size))
3515 return 0;
3516
3517 /*
3518 * In theory, objcg->nr_charged_bytes can have enough
3519 * pre-charged bytes to satisfy the allocation. However,
3520 * flushing objcg->nr_charged_bytes requires two atomic
3521 * operations, and objcg->nr_charged_bytes can't be big.
3522 * The shared objcg->nr_charged_bytes can also become a
3523 * performance bottleneck if all tasks of the same memcg are
3524 * trying to update it. So it's better to ignore it and try
3525 * grab some new pages. The stock's nr_bytes will be flushed to
3526 * objcg->nr_charged_bytes later on when objcg changes.
3527 *
3528 * The stock's nr_bytes may contain enough pre-charged bytes
3529 * to allow one less page from being charged, but we can't rely
3530 * on the pre-charged bytes not being changed outside of
3531 * consume_obj_stock() or refill_obj_stock(). So ignore those
3532 * pre-charged bytes as well when charging pages. To avoid a
3533 * page uncharge right after a page charge, we set the
3534 * allow_uncharge flag to false when calling refill_obj_stock()
3535 * to temporarily allow the pre-charged bytes to exceed the page
3536 * size limit. The maximum reachable value of the pre-charged
3537 * bytes is (sizeof(object) + PAGE_SIZE - 2) if there is no data
3538 * race.
3539 */
3540 nr_pages = size >> PAGE_SHIFT12;
3541 nr_bytes = size & (PAGE_SIZE((1UL) << 12) - 1);
3542
3543 if (nr_bytes)
3544 nr_pages += 1;
3545
3546 ret = obj_cgroup_charge_pages(objcg, gfp, nr_pages);
3547 if (!ret && nr_bytes)
3548 refill_obj_stock(objcg, PAGE_SIZE((1UL) << 12) - nr_bytes, false);
3549
3550 return ret;
3551}
3552
3553void obj_cgroup_uncharge(struct obj_cgroup *objcg, size_t size)
3554{
3555 refill_obj_stock(objcg, size, true);
3556}

3558static inlineinline __attribute__((__gnu_inline__)) __attribute__((__unused__
)) __attribute__((no_instrument_function)) size_t obj_full_size(struct kmem_cache *s)
3559{
3560 /*
3561 * For each accounted object there is an extra space which is used
3562 * to store obj_cgroup membership. Charge it too.
3563 */
3564 return s->size + sizeof(struct obj_cgroup *);

3567bool __memcg_slab_post_alloc_hook(struct kmem_cache *s, struct list_lru *lru,
3568 gfp_t flags, size_t size, void **p)
3569{
3570 struct obj_cgroup *objcg;
3571 struct slab *slab;
3572 unsigned long off;
3573 size_t i;
3574
3575 /*
3576 * The obtained objcg pointer is safe to use within the current scope,
3577 * defined by current task or set_active_memcg() pair.
3578 * obj_cgroup_get() is used to get a permanent reference.
3579 */
3580 objcg = current_obj_cgroup();
3581 if (!objcg)
3582 return true;
3583
3584 /*
3585 * slab_alloc_node() avoids the NULL check, so we might be called with a
3586 * single NULL object. kmem_cache_alloc_bulk() aborts if it can't fill
3587 * the whole requested size.
3588 * return success as there's nothing to free back
3589 */
3590 if (unlikely(*p == NULL)__builtin_expect(!!(*p == ((void *)0)), 0))
3591 return true;
3592
3593 flags &= gfp_allowed_mask;
3594
3595 if (lru) {
3596 int ret;
3597 struct mem_cgroup *memcg;
3598
3599 memcg = get_mem_cgroup_from_objcg(objcg);
3600 ret = memcg_list_lru_alloc(memcg, lru, flags);
3601 css_put(&memcg->css);
3602
3603 if (ret)
3604 return false;
3605 }
3606
3607 if (obj_cgroup_charge(objcg, flags, size * obj_full_size(s)))
3608 return false;
3609
3610 for (i = 0; i < size; i++) {
3611 slab = virt_to_slab(p[i]);
3612
3613 if (!slab_obj_exts(slab) &&
3614 alloc_slab_obj_exts(slab, s, flags, false)) {
3615 obj_cgroup_uncharge(objcg, obj_full_size(s));
3616 continue;
3617 }
3618
3619 off = obj_to_index(s, slab, p[i]);
3620 obj_cgroup_get(objcg);
3621 slab_obj_exts(slab)[off].objcg = objcg;
3622 mod_objcg_state(objcg, slab_pgdat(slab),
3623 cache_vmstat_idx(s), obj_full_size(s));
3624 }
3625
3626 return true;
3627}
3628
3629void __memcg_slab_free_hook(struct kmem_cache *s, struct slab *slab,
3630 void **p, int objects, struct slabobj_ext *obj_exts)
3631{
3632 for (int i = 0; i < objects; i++) {
3633 struct obj_cgroup *objcg;
3634 unsigned int off;
3635
3636 off = obj_to_index(s, slab, p[i]);
3637 objcg = obj_exts[off].objcg;
3638 if (!objcg)
3639 continue;
3640
3641 obj_exts[off].objcg = NULL((void *)0);
3642 obj_cgroup_uncharge(objcg, obj_full_size(s));
3643 mod_objcg_state(objcg, slab_pgdat(slab), cache_vmstat_idx(s),
3644 -obj_full_size(s));
3645 obj_cgroup_put(objcg);
3646 }
3647}

3697 mod_memcg_state(from, MEMCG_SWAP, -1);

3699 return 0;
3700 }
3701 return -EINVAL22;
3702}

3906static unsigned long mem_cgroup_usage(struct mem_cgroup *memcg, bool swap)
3907{
3908 unsigned long val;
3909
3910 if (mem_cgroup_is_root(memcg)) {
3911 /*
3912 * Approximate root's usage from global state. This isn't
3913 * perfect, but the root usage was always an approximation.
3914 */
3915 val = global_node_page_state(NR_FILE_PAGES) +
3916 global_node_page_state(NR_ANON_MAPPED);
3917 if (swap)
3918 val += total_swap_pages - get_nr_swap_pages();
3919 } else {
3920 if (!swap)
3921 val = page_counter_read(&memcg->memory);
3922 else
3923 val = page_counter_read(&memcg->memsw);
3924 }
3925 return val;
3926}

4050static int memcg_update_tcp_max(struct mem_cgroup *memcg, unsigned long max)
4051{
4052 int ret;
4053
4054 mutex_lock(&memcg_max_mutex)mutex_lock_nested(&memcg_max_mutex, 0);
4055
4056 ret = page_counter_set_max(&memcg->tcpmem, max);
4057 if (ret)
4058 goto out;
4059
4060 if (!memcg->tcpmem_active) {
4061 /*
4062 * The active flag needs to be written after the static_key
4063 * update. This is what guarantees that the socket activation
4064 * function is the last one to run. See mem_cgroup_sk_alloc()
4065 * for details, and note that we don't mark any socket as
4066 * belonging to this memcg until that flag is up.
4067 *
4068 * We need to do this, because static_keys will span multiple
4069 * sites, but we can't control their order. If we mark a socket
4070 * as accounted, but the accounting functions are not patched in
4071 * yet, we'll lose accounting.
4072 *
4073 * We never race with the readers in mem_cgroup_sk_alloc(),
4074 * because when this value change, the code to process it is not
4075 * patched in yet.
4076 */
4077 static_branch_inc(&memcg_sockets_enabled_key)static_key_slow_inc(&(&memcg_sockets_enabled_key)->
key);
4078 memcg->tcpmem_active = true;
4079 }
4080out:
4081 mutex_unlock(&memcg_max_mutex);
4082 return ret;
4083}

4505static int compare_thresholds(const void *a, const void *b)
4506{

4511 return 1;
4512
4513 if (_a->threshold < _b->threshold)
4514 return -1;
4515
4516 return 0;
4517}

4867/*
4868 * Foreign dirty flushing
4869 *
4870 * There's an inherent mismatch between memcg and writeback. The former
4871 * tracks ownership per-page while the latter per-inode. This was a
4872 * deliberate design decision because honoring per-page ownership in the
4873 * writeback path is complicated, may lead to higher CPU and IO overheads
4874 * and deemed unnecessary given that write-sharing an inode across
4875 * different cgroups isn't a common use-case.
4876 *
4877 * Combined with inode majority-writer ownership switching, this works well
4878 * enough in most cases but there are some pathological cases. For
4879 * example, let's say there are two cgroups A and B which keep writing to
4880 * different but confined parts of the same inode. B owns the inode and
4881 * A's memory is limited far below B's. A's dirty ratio can rise enough to
4882 * trigger balance_dirty_pages() sleeps but B's can be low enough to avoid
4883 * triggering background writeback. A will be slowed down without a way to
4884 * make writeback of the dirty pages happen.
4885 *
4886 * Conditions like the above can lead to a cgroup getting repeatedly and
4887 * severely throttled after making some progress after each
4888 * dirty_expire_interval while the underlying IO device is almost
4889 * completely idle.
4890 *
4891 * Solving this problem completely requires matching the ownership tracking
4892 * granularities between memcg and writeback in either direction. However,
4893 * the more egregious behaviors can be avoided by simply remembering the
4894 * most recent foreign dirtying events and initiating remote flushes on
4895 * them when local writeback isn't enough to keep the memory clean enough.
4896 *
4897 * The following two functions implement such mechanism. When a foreign
4898 * page - a page whose memcg and writeback ownerships don't match - is
4899 * dirtied, mem_cgroup_track_foreign_dirty() records the inode owning
4900 * bdi_writeback on the page owning memcg. When balance_dirty_pages()
4901 * decides that the memcg needs to sleep due to high dirty ratio, it calls
4902 * mem_cgroup_flush_foreign() which queues writeback on the recorded
4903 * foreign bdi_writebacks which haven't expired. Both the numbers of
4904 * recorded bdi_writebacks and concurrent in-flight foreign writebacks are
4905 * limited to MEMCG_CGWB_FRN_CNT.
4906 *
4907 * The mechanism only remembers IDs and doesn't hold any object references.
4908 * As being wrong occasionally doesn't matter, updates and accesses to the
4909 * records are lockless and racy.
4910 */

4929 frn = &memcg->cgwb_frn[i];
4930 if (frn->bdi_id == wb->bdi->id &&

5033
5034 event->unregister_event(memcg, event->eventfd);

5386/*
5387 * Private memory cgroup IDR
5388 *
5389 * Swap-out records and page cache shadow entries need to store memcg
5390 * references in constrained space, so we maintain an ID space that is
5391 * limited to 16 bit (MEM_CGROUP_ID_MAX), limiting the total number of
5392 * memory-controlled cgroups to 64k.
5393 *
5394 * However, there usually are many references to the offline CSS after
5395 * the cgroup has been destroyed, such as page cache or reclaimable
5396 * slab objects, that don't need to hang on to the ID. We want to keep
5397 * those dead CSS from occupying IDs, or we might quickly exhaust the
5398 * relatively small ID space and prevent the creation of new cgroups
5399 * even when there are much fewer than 64k cgroups - possibly none.
5400 *
5401 * Maintain a private 16-bit ID space for memcg, and allow the ID to
5402 * be freed and recycled when it's no longer needed, which is usually
5403 * when the CSS is offlined.
5404 *
5405 * The only exception to that are records of swapped out tmpfs/shmem
5406 * pages that need to be attributed to live ancestors on swapin. But
5407 * those references are manageable from userspace.
5408 */
5409
5410#define MEM_CGROUP_ID_MAX((1UL << 16) - 1) ((1UL << MEM_CGROUP_ID_SHIFT16) - 1)
5411static DEFINE_IDR(mem_cgroup_idr)struct idr mem_cgroup_idr = { .idr_rt = { .xa_lock = (spinlock_t
) { { .rlock = { .raw_lock = { { .val = { (0) } } }, .magic =
0xdead4ead, .owner_cpu = -1, .owner = ((void *)-1L), .dep_map
= { .name = "mem_cgroup_idr.xa_lock", .wait_type_inner = LD_WAIT_CONFIG
, } } } }, .xa_flags = ((( gfp_t)4) | ( gfp_t) (1 << ((
___GFP_LAST_BIT) + 0))), .xa_head = ((void *)0), }, .idr_base
= (0), .idr_next = 0, };
5412
5413static void mem_cgroup_id_remove(struct mem_cgroup *memcg)
5414{
5415 if (memcg->id.id > 0) {
5416 idr_remove(&mem_cgroup_idr, memcg->id.id);
5417 memcg->id.id = 0;
5418 }
5419}

5654static int mem_cgroup_css_online(struct cgroup_subsys_state *css)
5655{
5656 struct mem_cgroup *memcg = mem_cgroup_from_css(css);
5657
5658 if (memcg_online_kmem(memcg))
5659 goto remove_id;
5660
5661 /*
5662 * A memcg must be visible for expand_shrinker_info()
5663 * by the time the maps are allocated. So, we allocate maps
5664 * here, when for_each_mem_cgroup() can't skip it.
5665 */
5666 if (alloc_shrinker_info(memcg))
5667 goto offline_kmem;
5668
5669 if (unlikely(mem_cgroup_is_root(memcg))__builtin_expect(!!(mem_cgroup_is_root(memcg)), 0) && !mem_cgroup_disabled())
5670 queue_delayed_work(system_unbound_wq, &stats_flush_dwork,
5671 FLUSH_TIME(2UL*250));
5672 lru_gen_online_memcg(memcg);
5673
5674 /* Online state pins memcg ID, memcg ID pins CSS */
5675 refcount_set(&memcg->id.ref, 1);
5676 css_get(css);
5677
5678 /*
5679 * Ensure mem_cgroup_from_id() works once we're fully online.
5680 *
5681 * We could do this earlier and require callers to filter with
5682 * css_tryget_online(). But right now there are no users that
5683 * need earlier access, and the workingset code relies on the
5684 * cgroup tree linkage (mem_cgroup_get_nr_swap_pages()). So
5685 * publish it here at the end of onlining. This matches the
5686 * regular ID destruction during offlining.
5687 */
5688 idr_replace(&mem_cgroup_idr, memcg, memcg->id.id);
5689
5690 return 0;
5691offline_kmem:
5692 memcg_offline_kmem(memcg);
5693remove_id:
5694 mem_cgroup_id_remove(memcg);
5695 return -ENOMEM12;
5696}

5932static struct page *mc_handle_present_pte(struct vm_area_struct *vma,
5933 unsigned long addr, pte_t ptent)
5934{
5935 struct page *page = vm_normal_page(vma, addr, ptent);
5936
5937 if (!page)
5938 return NULL((void *)0);
5939 if (PageAnon(page)) {
5940 if (!(mc.flags & MOVE_ANON0x1U))
5941 return NULL((void *)0);
5942 } else {
5943 if (!(mc.flags & MOVE_FILE0x2U))
5944 return NULL((void *)0);
5945 }
5946 get_page(page);
5947
5948 return page;
5949}

5952static struct page *mc_handle_swap_pte(struct vm_area_struct *vma,
5953 pte_t ptent, swp_entry_t *entry)
5954{
5955 struct page *page = NULL((void *)0);
5956 swp_entry_t ent = pte_to_swp_entry(ptent);
5957
5958 if (!(mc.flags & MOVE_ANON0x1U))
5959 return NULL((void *)0);
5960
5961 /*
5962 * Handle device private pages that are not accessible by the CPU, but
5963 * stored as special swap entries in the page table.
5964 */
5965 if (is_device_private_entry(ent)) {
5966 page = pfn_swap_entry_to_page(ent);
5967 if (!get_page_unless_zero(page))
5968 return NULL((void *)0);
5969 return page;
5970 }
5971
5972 if (non_swap_entry(ent))
5973 return NULL((void *)0);
5974
5975 /*
5976 * Because swap_cache_get_folio() updates some statistics counter,
5977 * we call find_get_page() with swapper_space directly.
5978 */
5979 page = find_get_page(swap_address_space(ent)(&swapper_spaces[swp_type(ent)][swp_offset(ent) >> 14
]), swp_offset(ent));
5980 entry->val = ent.val;
5981
5982 return page;
5983}

5992static struct page *mc_handle_file_pte(struct vm_area_struct *vma,
5993 unsigned long addr, pte_t ptent)
5994{
5995 unsigned long index;
5996 struct folio *folio;
5997
5998 if (!vma->vm_file) /* anonymous vma */
5999 return NULL((void *)0);
6000 if (!(mc.flags & MOVE_FILE0x2U))
6001 return NULL((void *)0);
6002
6003 /* folio is moved even if it's not RSS of this task(page-faulted). */
6004 /* shmem/tmpfs may report page out on swap: account for that too. */
6005 index = linear_page_index(vma, addr);
6006 folio = filemap_get_incore_folio(vma->vm_file->f_mapping, index);
6007 if (IS_ERR(folio))
6008 return NULL((void *)0);
6009 return folio_file_page(folio, index);
6010}

6132/**
6133 * get_mctgt_type - get target type of moving charge
6134 * @vma: the vma the pte to be checked belongs
6135 * @addr: the address corresponding to the pte to be checked
6136 * @ptent: the pte to be checked
6137 * @target: the pointer the target page or swap ent will be stored(can be NULL)
6138 *
6139 * Context: Called with pte lock held.
6140 * Return:
6141 * * MC_TARGET_NONE - If the pte is not a target for move charge.
6142 * * MC_TARGET_PAGE - If the page corresponding to this pte is a target for
6143 * move charge. If @target is not NULL, the folio is stored in target->folio
6144 * with extra refcnt taken (Caller should release it).
6145 * * MC_TARGET_SWAP - If the swap entry corresponding to this pte is a
6146 * target for charge migration. If @target is not NULL, the entry is
6147 * stored in target->ent.
6148 * * MC_TARGET_DEVICE - Like MC_TARGET_PAGE but page is device memory and
6149 * thus not on the lru. For now such page is charged like a regular page
6150 * would be as it is just special memory taking the place of a regular page.
6151 * See Documentations/vm/hmm.txt and include/linux/hmm.h
6152 */
6153static enum mc_target_type get_mctgt_type(struct vm_area_struct *vma,
6154 unsigned long addr, pte_t ptent, union mc_target *target)
6155{
6156 struct page *page = NULL((void *)0);
6157 struct folio *folio;
6158 enum mc_target_type ret = MC_TARGET_NONE;
6159 swp_entry_t ent = { .val = 0 };
6160
6161 if (pte_present(ptent))
6162 page = mc_handle_present_pte(vma, addr, ptent);
6163 else if (pte_none_mostly(ptent))
6164 /*
6165 * PTE markers should be treated as a none pte here, separated
6166 * from other swap handling below.
6167 */
6168 page = mc_handle_file_pte(vma, addr, ptent);
6169 else if (is_swap_pte(ptent))
6170 page = mc_handle_swap_pte(vma, ptent, &ent);
6171
6172 if (page)
6173 folio = page_folio(page)(_Generic((page), const struct page *: (const struct folio *)
_compound_head(page), struct page *: (struct folio *)_compound_head
(page)));
6174 if (target && page) {
6175 if (!folio_trylock(folio)) {
6176 folio_put(folio);
6177 return ret;
6178 }
6179 /*
6180 * page_mapped() must be stable during the move. This
6181 * pte is locked, so if it's present, the page cannot
6182 * become unmapped. If it isn't, we have only partial
6183 * control over the mapped state: the page lock will
6184 * prevent new faults against pagecache and swapcache,
6185 * so an unmapped page cannot become mapped. However,
6186 * if the page is already mapped elsewhere, it can
6187 * unmap, and there is nothing we can do about it.
6188 * Alas, skip moving the page in this case.
6189 */
6190 if (!pte_present(ptent) && page_mapped(page)) {
6191 folio_unlock(folio);
6192 folio_put(folio);
6193 return ret;
6194 }
6195 }
6196
6197 if (!page && !ent.val)
6198 return ret;
6199 if (page) {
6200 /*
6201 * Do only loose check w/o serialization.
6202 * mem_cgroup_move_account() checks the page is valid or
6203 * not under LRU exclusion.
6204 */
6205 if (folio_memcg(folio) == mc.from) {
6206 ret = MC_TARGET_PAGE;
6207 if (folio_is_device_private(folio) ||
6208 folio_is_device_coherent(folio))
6209 ret = MC_TARGET_DEVICE;
6210 if (target)
6211 target->folio = folio;
6212 }
6213 if (!ret || !target) {
6214 if (target)
6215 folio_unlock(folio);
6216 folio_put(folio);
6217 }
6218 }
6219 /*
6220 * There is a swap entry and a page doesn't exist or isn't charged.
6221 * But we cannot move a tail-page in a THP.
6222 */
6223 if (ent.val && !ret && (!page || !PageTransCompound(page)) &&
6224 mem_cgroup_id(mc.from) == lookup_swap_cgroup_id(ent)) {
6225 ret = MC_TARGET_SWAP;
6226 if (target)
6227 target->ent = ent;
6228 }
6229 return ret;
6230}

6276static int mem_cgroup_count_precharge_pte_range(pmd_t *pmd,
6277 unsigned long addr, unsigned long end,
6278 struct mm_walk *walk)
6279{
6280 struct vm_area_struct *vma = walk->vma;
6281 pte_t *pte;
6282 spinlock_t *ptl;
6283
6284 ptl = pmd_trans_huge_lock(pmd, vma);
6285 if (ptl) {
6286 /*
6287 * Note their can not be MC_TARGET_DEVICE for now as we do not
6288 * support transparent huge page with MEMORY_DEVICE_PRIVATE but
6289 * this might change.
6290 */
6291 if (get_mctgt_type_thp(vma, addr, *pmd, NULL((void *)0)) == MC_TARGET_PAGE)
6292 mc.precharge += HPAGE_PMD_NR(1<<(21 -12));
6293 spin_unlock(ptl);
6294 return 0;
6295 }
6296
6297 pte = pte_offset_map_lock(vma->vm_mm, pmd, addr, &ptl);
6298 if (!pte)
6299 return 0;
6300 for (; addr != end; pte++, addr += PAGE_SIZE((1UL) << 12))
6301 if (get_mctgt_type(vma, addr, ptep_get(pte), NULL((void *)0)))
6302 mc.precharge++; /* increment precharge temporarily */
6303 pte_unmap_unlock(pte - 1, ptl)do { spin_unlock(ptl); pte_unmap(pte - 1); } while (0);
6304 cond_resched()({ __might_resched("mm/memcontrol.c", 6304, 0); _cond_resched
(); });
6305
6306 return 0;
6307}
6308
6309static const struct mm_walk_ops precharge_walk_ops = {
6310 .pmd_entry = mem_cgroup_count_precharge_pte_range,
6311 .walk_lock = PGWALK_RDLOCK,
6312};
6313
6314static unsigned long mem_cgroup_count_precharge(struct mm_struct *mm)
6315{
6316 unsigned long precharge;
6317
6318 mmap_read_lock(mm);
6319 walk_page_range(mm, 0, ULONG_MAX(~0UL), &precharge_walk_ops, NULL((void *)0));
6320 mmap_read_unlock(mm);
6321
6322 precharge = mc.precharge;
6323 mc.precharge = 0;
6324
6325 return precharge;
6326}

6337/* cancels all extra charges on mc.from and mc.to, and wakes up all waiters. */
6338static void __mem_cgroup_clear_mc(void)
6339{
6340 struct mem_cgroup *from = mc.from;
6341 struct mem_cgroup *to = mc.to;
6342
6343 /* we must uncharge all the leftover precharges from mc.to */
6344 if (mc.precharge) {
6345 mem_cgroup_cancel_charge(mc.to, mc.precharge);
6346 mc.precharge = 0;
6347 }
6348 /*
6349 * we didn't uncharge from mc.from at mem_cgroup_move_account(), so
6350 * we must uncharge here.
6351 */
6352 if (mc.moved_charge) {
6353 mem_cgroup_cancel_charge(mc.from, mc.moved_charge);
6354 mc.moved_charge = 0;
6355 }
6356 /* we must fixup refcnts and charges */
6357 if (mc.moved_swap) {
6358 /* uncharge swap account from the old cgroup */
6359 if (!mem_cgroup_is_root(mc.from))
6360 page_counter_uncharge(&mc.from->memsw, mc.moved_swap);
6361
6362 mem_cgroup_id_put_many(mc.from, mc.moved_swap);
6363
6364 /*
6365 * we charged both to->memory and to->memsw, so we
6366 * should uncharge to->memory.
6367 */
6368 if (!mem_cgroup_is_root(mc.to))
6369 page_counter_uncharge(&mc.to->memory, mc.moved_swap);
6370
6371 mc.moved_swap = 0;
6372 }
6373 memcg_oom_recover(from);
6374 memcg_oom_recover(to);
6375 wake_up_all(&mc.waitq)__wake_up(&mc.waitq, (0x00000001 | 0x00000002), 0, ((void
*)0));
6376}

6378static void mem_cgroup_clear_mc(void)
6379{
6380 struct mm_struct *mm = mc.mm;
6381
6382 /*
6383 * we must clear moving_task before waking up waiters at the end of
6384 * task migration.
6385 */
6386 mc.moving_task = NULL((void *)0);
6387 __mem_cgroup_clear_mc();
6388 spin_lock(&mc.lock);
6389 mc.from = NULL((void *)0);
6390 mc.to = NULL((void *)0);
6391 mc.mm = NULL((void *)0);
6392 spin_unlock(&mc.lock);
6393
6394 mmput(mm);
6395}

6473static int mem_cgroup_move_charge_pte_range(pmd_t *pmd,
6474 unsigned long addr, unsigned long end,
6475 struct mm_walk *walk)
6476{
6477 int ret = 0;
6478 struct vm_area_struct *vma = walk->vma;
6479 pte_t *pte;
6480 spinlock_t *ptl;
6481 enum mc_target_type target_type;
6482 union mc_target target;
6483 struct folio *folio;
6484
6485 ptl = pmd_trans_huge_lock(pmd, vma);
6486 if (ptl) {
6487 if (mc.precharge < HPAGE_PMD_NR(1<<(21 -12))) {
6488 spin_unlock(ptl);
6489 return 0;
6490 }
6491 target_type = get_mctgt_type_thp(vma, addr, *pmd, &target);
6492 if (target_type == MC_TARGET_PAGE) {
6493 folio = target.folio;
6494 if (folio_isolate_lru(folio)) {
6495 if (!mem_cgroup_move_account(folio, true,
6496 mc.from, mc.to)) {
6497 mc.precharge -= HPAGE_PMD_NR(1<<(21 -12));
6498 mc.moved_charge += HPAGE_PMD_NR(1<<(21 -12));
6499 }
6500 folio_putback_lru(folio);
6501 }
6502 folio_unlock(folio);
6503 folio_put(folio);
6504 } else if (target_type == MC_TARGET_DEVICE) {
6505 folio = target.folio;
6506 if (!mem_cgroup_move_account(folio, true,
6507 mc.from, mc.to)) {
6508 mc.precharge -= HPAGE_PMD_NR(1<<(21 -12));
6509 mc.moved_charge += HPAGE_PMD_NR(1<<(21 -12));
6510 }
6511 folio_unlock(folio);
6512 folio_put(folio);
6513 }
6514 spin_unlock(ptl);
6515 return 0;
6516 }
6517
6518retry:
6519 pte = pte_offset_map_lock(vma->vm_mm, pmd, addr, &ptl);
6520 if (!pte)
6521 return 0;
6522 for (; addr != end; addr += PAGE_SIZE((1UL) << 12)) {
6523 pte_t ptent = ptep_get(pte++);
6524 bool device = false;
6525 swp_entry_t ent;
6526
6527 if (!mc.precharge)
6528 break;
6529
6530 switch (get_mctgt_type(vma, addr, ptent, &target)) {
6531 case MC_TARGET_DEVICE:
6532 device = true;
6533 fallthrough__attribute__((__fallthrough__));
6534 case MC_TARGET_PAGE:
6535 folio = target.folio;
6536 /*
6537 * We can have a part of the split pmd here. Moving it
6538 * can be done but it would be too convoluted so simply
6539 * ignore such a partial THP and keep it in original
6540 * memcg. There should be somebody mapping the head.
6541 */
6542 if (folio_test_large(folio))
6543 goto put;
6544 if (!device && !folio_isolate_lru(folio))
6545 goto put;
6546 if (!mem_cgroup_move_account(folio, false,
6547 mc.from, mc.to)) {
6548 mc.precharge--;
6549 /* we uncharge from mc.from later. */
6550 mc.moved_charge++;
6551 }
6552 if (!device)
6553 folio_putback_lru(folio);
6554put: /* get_mctgt_type() gets & locks the page */
6555 folio_unlock(folio);
6556 folio_put(folio);
6557 break;
6558 case MC_TARGET_SWAP:
6559 ent = target.ent;
6560 if (!mem_cgroup_move_swap_account(ent, mc.from, mc.to)) {
6561 mc.precharge--;
6562 mem_cgroup_id_get_many(mc.to, 1);
6563 /* we fixup other refcnts and charges later. */
6564 mc.moved_swap++;
6565 }
6566 break;
6567 default:
6568 break;
6569 }
6570 }
6571 pte_unmap_unlock(pte - 1, ptl)do { spin_unlock(ptl); pte_unmap(pte - 1); } while (0);
6572 cond_resched()({ __might_resched("mm/memcontrol.c", 6572, 0); _cond_resched
(); });
6573
6574 if (addr != end) {
6575 /*
6576 * We have consumed all precharges we got in can_attach().
6577 * We try charge one by one, but don't do any additional
6578 * charges to mc.to if we have failed in charge once in attach()
6579 * phase.
6580 */
6581 ret = mem_cgroup_do_precharge(1);
6582 if (!ret)
6583 goto retry;
6584 }
6585
6586 return ret;
6587}

6589static const struct mm_walk_ops charge_walk_ops = {
6590 .pmd_entry = mem_cgroup_move_charge_pte_range,
6591 .walk_lock = PGWALK_RDLOCK,
6592};
6593
6594static void mem_cgroup_move_charge(void)
6595{
6596 lru_add_drain_all();
6597 /*
6598 * Signal folio_memcg_lock() to take the memcg's move_lock
6599 * while we're moving its pages to another memcg. Then wait
6600 * for already started RCU-only updates to finish.
6601 */
6602 atomic_inc(&mc.from->moving_account);
6603 synchronize_rcu();
6604retry:
6605 if (unlikely(!mmap_read_trylock(mc.mm))__builtin_expect(!!(!mmap_read_trylock(mc.mm)), 0)) {
6606 /*
6607 * Someone who are holding the mmap_lock might be waiting in
6608 * waitq. So we cancel all extra charges, wake up all waiters,
6609 * and retry. Because we cancel precharges, we might not be able
6610 * to move enough charges, but moving charge is a best-effort
6611 * feature anyway, so it wouldn't be a big problem.
6612 */
6613 __mem_cgroup_clear_mc();
6614 cond_resched()({ __might_resched("mm/memcontrol.c", 6614, 0); _cond_resched
(); });
6615 goto retry;
6616 }
6617 /*
6618 * When we have consumed all precharges and failed in doing
6619 * additional charge, the page walk just aborts.
6620 */
6621 walk_page_range(mc.mm, 0, ULONG_MAX(~0UL), &charge_walk_ops, NULL((void *)0));
6622 mmap_read_unlock(mc.mm);
6623 atomic_dec(&mc.from->moving_account);
6624}

6626static void mem_cgroup_move_task(void)
6627{
6628 if (mc.to) {
6629 mem_cgroup_move_charge();
6630 mem_cgroup_clear_mc();
6631 }
6632}

6648static void mem_cgroup_fork(struct task_struct *task)
6649{
6650 /*
6651 * Set the update flag to cause task->objcg to be initialized lazily
6652 * on the first allocation. It can be done without any synchronization
6653 * because it's always performed on the current task, so does
6654 * current_objcg_update().
6655 */
6656 task->objcg = (struct obj_cgroup *)CURRENT_OBJCG_UPDATE_FLAG(1UL << 0);
6657}

6659static void mem_cgroup_exit(struct task_struct *task)
6660{
6661 struct obj_cgroup *objcg = task->objcg;
6662
6663 objcg = (struct obj_cgroup *)
6664 ((unsigned long)objcg & ~CURRENT_OBJCG_UPDATE_FLAG(1UL << 0));
6665 obj_cgroup_put(objcg);
6666
6667 /*
6668 * Some kernel allocations can happen after this point,
6669 * but let's ignore them. It can be done without any synchronization
6670 * because it's always performed on the current task, so does
6671 * current_objcg_update().
6672 */
6673 task->objcg = NULL((void *)0);
6674}

7012static ssize_t memory_reclaim(struct kernfs_open_file *of, char *buf,
7013 size_t nbytes, loff_t off)

7023 if (err)

7026 reclaim_options = MEMCG_RECLAIM_MAY_SWAP(1 << 1) | MEMCG_RECLAIM_PROACTIVE(1 << 2);
7027 while (nr_reclaimed < nr_to_reclaim) {
7028 /* Will converge on zero, but reclaim enforces a minimum */
7029 unsigned long batch_size = (nr_to_reclaim - nr_reclaimed) / 4;
7030 unsigned long reclaimed;
7031
7032 if (signal_pending(currentget_current()))
7033 return -EINTR4;
7034
7035 /*
7036 * This is the final attempt, drain percpu lru caches in the
7037 * hope of introducing more evictable pages for
7038 * try_to_free_mem_cgroup_pages().
7039 */

7044 batch_size, GFP_KERNEL((( gfp_t)(((((1UL))) << (___GFP_DIRECT_RECLAIM_BIT))|(
(((1UL))) << (___GFP_KSWAPD_RECLAIM_BIT)))) | (( gfp_t)
((((1UL))) << (___GFP_IO_BIT))) | (( gfp_t)((((1UL))) <<
(___GFP_FS_BIT)))), reclaim_options);
7045
7046 if (!reclaimed && !nr_retries--)
7047 return -EAGAIN11;
7048
7049 nr_reclaimed += reclaimed;
7050 }
7051
7052 return nbytes;
7053}

7149/*
7150 * This function calculates an individual cgroup's effective
7151 * protection which is derived from its own memory.min/low, its
7152 * parent's and siblings' settings, as well as the actual memory
7153 * distribution in the tree.
7154 *
7155 * The following rules apply to the effective protection values:
7156 *
7157 * 1. At the first level of reclaim, effective protection is equal to
7158 * the declared protection in memory.min and memory.low.
7159 *
7160 * 2. To enable safe delegation of the protection configuration, at
7161 * subsequent levels the effective protection is capped to the
7162 * parent's effective protection.
7163 *
7164 * 3. To make complex and dynamic subtrees easier to configure, the
7165 * user is allowed to overcommit the declared protection at a given
7166 * level. If that is the case, the parent's effective protection is
7167 * distributed to the children in proportion to how much protection
7168 * they have declared and how much of it they are utilizing.
7169 *
7170 * This makes distribution proportional, but also work-conserving:
7171 * if one cgroup claims much more protection than it uses memory,
7172 * the unused remainder is available to its siblings.
7173 *
7174 * 4. Conversely, when the declared protection is undercommitted at a
7175 * given level, the distribution of the larger parental protection
7176 * budget is NOT proportional. A cgroup's protection from a sibling
7177 * is capped to its own memory.min/low setting.
7178 *
7179 * 5. However, to allow protecting recursive subtrees from each other
7180 * without having to declare each individual cgroup's fixed share
7181 * of the ancestor's claim to protection, any unutilized -
7182 * "floating" - protection from up the tree is distributed in
7183 * proportion to each cgroup's *usage*. This makes the protection
7184 * neutral wrt sibling cgroups and lets them compete freely over
7185 * the shared parental protection budget, but it protects the
7186 * subtree as a whole from neighboring subtrees.
7187 *
7188 * Note that 4. and 5. are not in conflict: 4. is about protecting
7189 * against immediate siblings whereas 5. is about protecting against
7190 * neighboring subtrees.
7191 */
7192static unsigned long effective_protection(unsigned long usage,
7193 unsigned long parent_usage,
7194 unsigned long setting,
7195 unsigned long parent_effective,
7196 unsigned long siblings_protected)
7197{
7198 unsigned long protected;
7199 unsigned long ep;
7200

7202 /*
7203 * If all cgroups at this level combined claim and use more
7204 * protection than what the parent affords them, distribute
7205 * shares in proportion to utilization.
7206 *
7207 * We are using actual utilization rather than the statically
7208 * claimed protection in order to be work-conserving: claimed
7209 * but unused protection is available to siblings that would
7210 * otherwise get a smaller chunk than what they claimed.
7211 */
7212 if (siblings_protected > parent_effective)
7213 return protected * parent_effective / siblings_protected;
7214
7215 /*
7216 * Ok, utilized protection of all children is within what the
7217 * parent affords them, so we know whatever this child claims
7218 * and utilizes is effectively protected.
7219 *
7220 * If there is unprotected usage beyond this value, reclaim
7221 * will apply pressure in proportion to that amount.
7222 *
7223 * If there is unutilized protection, the cgroup will be fully
7224 * shielded from reclaim, but we do return a smaller value for
7225 * protection than what the group could enjoy in theory. This
7226 * is okay. With the overcommit distribution above, effective
7227 * protection is always dependent on how memory is actually
7228 * consumed among the siblings anyway.
7229 */
7230 ep = protected;
7231
7232 /*
7233 * If the children aren't claiming (all of) the protection
7234 * afforded to them by the parent, distribute the remainder in
7235 * proportion to the (unprotected) memory of each cgroup. That
7236 * way, cgroups that aren't explicitly prioritized wrt each
7237 * other compete freely over the allowance, but they are
7238 * collectively protected from neighboring trees.
7239 *
7240 * We're using unprotected memory for the weight so that if
7241 * some cgroups DO claim explicit protection, we don't protect
7242 * the same bytes twice.
7243 *
7244 * Check both usage and parent_usage against the respective
7245 * protected values. One should imply the other, but they
7246 * aren't read atomically - make sure the division is sane.
7247 */
7248 if (!(cgrp_dfl_root.flags & CGRP_ROOT_MEMORY_RECURSIVE_PROT))
7249 return ep;
7250 if (parent_effective > siblings_protected &&
7251 parent_usage > siblings_protected &&
7252 usage > protected) {
7253 unsigned long unclaimed;
7254
7255 unclaimed = parent_effective - siblings_protected;
7256 unclaimed *= usage - protected;
7257 unclaimed /= parent_usage - siblings_protected;
7258
7259 ep += unclaimed;
7260 }
7261
7262 return ep;
7263}

7320static int charge_memcg(struct folio *folio, struct mem_cgroup *memcg,
7321 gfp_t gfp)
7322{
7323 int ret;
7324
7325 ret = try_charge(memcg, gfp, folio_nr_pages(folio));
7326 if (ret)
7327 goto out;
7328
7329 mem_cgroup_commit_charge(folio, memcg);
7330out:
7331 return ret;
7332}
7333
7334int __mem_cgroup_charge(struct folio *folio, struct mm_struct *mm, gfp_t gfp)
7335{
7336 struct mem_cgroup *memcg;
7337 int ret;
7338
7339 memcg = get_mem_cgroup_from_mm(mm);
7340 ret = charge_memcg(folio, memcg, gfp);
7341 css_put(&memcg->css);
7342
7343 return ret;
7344}

7346/**
7347 * mem_cgroup_hugetlb_try_charge - try to charge the memcg for a hugetlb folio
7348 * @memcg: memcg to charge.
7349 * @gfp: reclaim mode.
7350 * @nr_pages: number of pages to charge.
7351 *
7352 * This function is called when allocating a huge page folio to determine if
7353 * the memcg has the capacity for it. It does not commit the charge yet,
7354 * as the hugetlb folio itself has not been obtained from the hugetlb pool.
7355 *
7356 * Once we have obtained the hugetlb folio, we can call
7357 * mem_cgroup_commit_charge() to commit the charge. If we fail to obtain the
7358 * folio, we should instead call mem_cgroup_cancel_charge() to undo the effect
7359 * of try_charge().
7360 *
7361 * Returns 0 on success. Otherwise, an error code is returned.
7362 */
7363int mem_cgroup_hugetlb_try_charge(struct mem_cgroup *memcg, gfp_t gfp,
7364 long nr_pages)
7365{
7366 /*
7367 * If hugetlb memcg charging is not enabled, do not fail hugetlb allocation,
7368 * but do not attempt to commit charge later (or cancel on error) either.
7369 */
7370 if (mem_cgroup_disabled() || !memcg ||
7371 !cgroup_subsys_on_dfl(memory_cgrp_subsys)({ bool branch; if (__builtin_types_compatible_p(typeof(*&
memory_cgrp_subsys_on_dfl_key), struct static_key_true)) branch
= !arch_static_branch(&(&memory_cgrp_subsys_on_dfl_key
)->key, true); else if (__builtin_types_compatible_p(typeof
(*&memory_cgrp_subsys_on_dfl_key), struct static_key_false
)) branch = !arch_static_branch_jump(&(&memory_cgrp_subsys_on_dfl_key
)->key, true); else branch = ____wrong_branch_error(); __builtin_expect
(!!(branch), 1); }) ||
7372 !(cgrp_dfl_root.flags & CGRP_ROOT_MEMORY_HUGETLB_ACCOUNTING))
7373 return -EOPNOTSUPP95;
7374
7375 if (try_charge(memcg, gfp, nr_pages))
7376 return -ENOMEM12;
7377
7378 return 0;
7379}

7381/**
7382 * mem_cgroup_swapin_charge_folio - Charge a newly allocated folio for swapin.
7383 * @folio: folio to charge.
7384 * @mm: mm context of the victim
7385 * @gfp: reclaim mode
7386 * @entry: swap entry for which the folio is allocated
7387 *
7388 * This function charges a folio allocated for swapin. Please call this before
7389 * adding the folio to the swapcache.
7390 *
7391 * Returns 0 on success. Otherwise, an error code is returned.
7392 */
7393int mem_cgroup_swapin_charge_folio(struct folio *folio, struct mm_struct *mm,
7394 gfp_t gfp, swp_entry_t entry)
7395{
7396 struct mem_cgroup *memcg;
7397 unsigned short id;
7398 int ret;
7399
7400 if (mem_cgroup_disabled())
7401 return 0;
7402
7403 id = lookup_swap_cgroup_id(entry);
7404 rcu_read_lock();
7405 memcg = mem_cgroup_from_id(id);
7406 if (!memcg || !css_tryget_online(&memcg->css))
7407 memcg = get_mem_cgroup_from_mm(mm);
7408 rcu_read_unlock();
7409
7410 ret = charge_memcg(folio, memcg, gfp);
7411
7412 css_put(&memcg->css);
7413 return ret;
7414}
7415
7416/*
7417 * mem_cgroup_swapin_uncharge_swap - uncharge swap slot
7418 * @entry: swap entry for which the page is charged
7419 *
7420 * Call this function after successfully adding the charged page to swapcache.
7421 *
7422 * Note: This function assumes the page for which swap slot is being uncharged
7423 * is order 0 page.
7424 */
7425void mem_cgroup_swapin_uncharge_swap(swp_entry_t entry)
7426{
7427 /*
7428 * Cgroup1's unified memory+swap counter has been charged with the
7429 * new swapcache page, finish the transfer by uncharging the swap
7430 * slot. The swap slot would also get uncharged when it dies, but
7431 * it can stick around indefinitely and we'd count the page twice
7432 * the entire time.
7433 *
7434 * Cgroup2 has separate resource counters for memory and swap,
7435 * so this is a non-issue here. Memory and swap charge lifetimes
7436 * correspond 1:1 to page and swap slot lifetimes: we charge the
7437 * page to memory here, and uncharge swap when the slot is freed.
7438 */
7439 if (!mem_cgroup_disabled() && do_memsw_account()) {
7440 /*
7441 * The swap entry might not get freed for a long time,
7442 * let's not wait for it. The page already received a
7443 * memory+swap charge, drop the swap entry duplicate.
7444 */
7445 mem_cgroup_uncharge_swap(entry, 1);
7446 }
7447}

7547void __mem_cgroup_uncharge(struct folio *folio)
7548{
7549 struct uncharge_gather ug;
7550
7551 /* Don't touch folio->lru of any random page, pre-check: */
7552 if (!folio_memcg(folio))
7553 return;
7554
7555 uncharge_gather_clear(&ug);
7556 uncharge_folio(folio, &ug);
7557 uncharge_batch(&ug);
7558}
7559
7560void __mem_cgroup_uncharge_folios(struct folio_batch *folios)
7561{
7562 struct uncharge_gather ug;
7563 unsigned int i;
7564
7565 uncharge_gather_clear(&ug);
7566 for (i = 0; i < folios->nr; i++)
7567 uncharge_folio(folios->folios[i], &ug);
7568 if (ug.memcg)
7569 uncharge_batch(&ug);
7570}

7957void __mem_cgroup_uncharge_swap(swp_entry_t entry, unsigned int nr_pages)
7958{
7959 struct mem_cgroup *memcg;

7962 id = swap_cgroup_record(entry, 0, nr_pages);

7973 mem_cgroup_id_put_many(memcg, nr_pages);
7974 }
7975 rcu_read_unlock();
7976}
